subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist an OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and reconcile `ai.openclaw.mac` after startup or Sparkle update drift, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd state as authoritative, while the report asks for enabled user intent to survive app replacement; changing that behavior can restore intent but may also override an intentional external disable.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
options.body: Store explicit app-owned enabled intent and re-register only the OpenClaw app LaunchAgent when startup or update checks prove the app-owned registration drifted.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave the toggle as a live launchd/System Settings reflection and document that OpenClaw does not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Keep implementation parked until a current-main Sparkle update reproduction identifies exactly which state flips.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit app-owned enabled intent and re-register only the OpenClaw app LaunchAgent when startup or update checks prove the app-owned registration drifted.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for prior Launch at Login source-of-truth work and the OpenClaw-named macOS LaunchAgent path points to steipete.
